requirements.title: Assignment has snapshot evaluation effects
requirements.definition: Assign the appropriately converted expression value with effects equivalent to evaluating the RHS and the expressions in the LHS designator before any destination portion is defined. References to the destination within either side are permitted, subject to -002 and the expression rules.
requirements.oracle: Compare with an independently specified pre-assignment result. Include scalar, section, and whole-array cases; do not assert evaluation order or that a temporary was physically created. -014 through -022 and -024 through -032 refine the conversion and derived-type effects.

requirements.title: The two sides' evaluations are independent
requirements.definition: Evaluation of expressions in the LHS designator must not affect, or be affected by, evaluation of the RHS.

pending.lhs-affects-rhs: Needs a separately specified diagnostic-policy tier.
pending.rhs-affects-lhs: Needs a separately specified diagnostic-policy tier.

requirements.oracle: Run only the conforming controls in the conformance tier. For a proposed diagnostic-policy violation, record the interfering state and a minimal repair that removes the interference. Other expression restrictions may also apply; an arbitrary execution order is not an oracle for a violating program.

requirements.title: Assignment through a pointer defines its target
requirements.definition: With a pointer LHS, intrinsic assignment writes the expression value to its target rather than performing pointer assignment.
requirements.oracle: Check target values and the continuing association to the original live target. Use an associated, definable target satisfying 10.2.1.2; an unassociated pointer is not a valid control.

requirements.title: An unallocated array cannot acquire shape from a scalar
requirements.definition: If the allocatable LHS array is unallocated, the RHS must have the same rank.

pending.unallocated-scalar-rhs: No unconditional diagnostic or runtime trap is required here.

requirements.oracle: The positive unallocated case uses a conforming same-rank array RHS. The isolated scalar-RHS violation is repaired by allocating the LHS first. Do not require a compile-time error for an allocation state that is only known at runtime, or execute the violation as a required-failure test.

requirements.title: Assignment deallocates an incompatible existing allocation
requirements.definition: An allocated allocatable destination is deallocated when an array RHS differs in shape, corresponding length parameters differ, or, for a polymorphic destination, the dynamic type or corresponding kind parameters differ.
requirements.oracle: Use eligible assignments that isolate each trigger, then check the characteristics and values specified by -006 through -011. The no-trigger control checks preservation of observable destination bounds. Do not test storage-address changes or inspect a pointer made undefined by deallocation. Lifecycle-sensitive cases also need the finalization rules.

requirements.title: An unallocated allocatable destination is allocated
requirements.source: p3, allocation lead-in following the deallocation conditions.
requirements.definition: An eligible allocatable destination that is initially unallocated, or becomes unallocated during assignment, is allocated before receiving the assigned value.
requirements.oracle: Check allocation status and the assigned value separately. An allocated zero-sized array is not the same state as an unallocated array. Allocation characteristics are covered by the following entries.

requirements.title: Polymorphic allocation takes the RHS type and kind
requirements.definition: Allocation of a polymorphic assignment destination uses the dynamic type and kind parameters of the RHS.
requirements.oracle: Establish the resulting dynamic type, kind parameters, and payload using appropriate type guards and inquiries. Do not infer the dynamic type from equal payload values alone. Keep length and shape unchanged when isolating the type/kind facets.

requirements.title: Allocation establishes deferred type parameters
requirements.definition: Each deferred type parameter of the allocated destination is established from the corresponding RHS parameter.
requirements.oracle: Check the parameter values as well as the payload. This does not make a nondeferred parameter changeable. Compare a whole allocatable character assignment with an already allocated substring assignment to separate allocation from ordinary truncation/padding.

requirements.title: Scalar-RHS reallocation retains previous array bounds
requirements.definition: If an existing allocatable array is reallocated for an assignment with a scalar RHS, its allocation retains the previous bounds.
requirements.oracle: Start with an allocated array, capture its observable bounds, and trigger an eligible length or type change with a scalar RHS. Check the bounds, new characteristics, and scalar expansion. An initially unallocated array with a scalar RHS instead violates -004.

requirements.title: Array-RHS allocation takes the RHS shape
requirements.definition: When an allocatable destination is allocated during an array-RHS assignment, the allocation has the RHS shape.
requirements.oracle: Check every extent, not merely total size or rank. Use distinguishable element values to check subsequent assignment separately under -013. Same-shape assignment to an existing allocation is a separate control, not evidence of a new allocation.

requirements.title: Array-RHS allocation uses expression lower bounds
requirements.definition: Each lower bound of the destination allocated for an array RHS is obtained from the corresponding element of `LBOUND(expr)`.
requirements.oracle: Use independently known bounds and the rules of 16.9.119. Do not substitute the bounds of a source object's declaration for those of an expression. Empty dimensions require particular care. In a no-trigger control, differently based but same-shaped arrays do not imply that the existing destination must adopt the RHS bounds.

requirements.title: A scalar RHS expands over the destination shape
requirements.definition: An eligible scalar-to-array assignment has the effect of assigning the scalar value to every element of the destination shape.
requirements.oracle: Check all selected elements and untouched surrounding elements. Combine a scalar derived from the old destination with -001. Do not interpret expansion as permission to allocate an initially unallocated array from a scalar.

requirements.title: Array assignment pairs corresponding elements
requirements.definition: Array intrinsic assignment assigns corresponding elements of the destination and RHS, without prescribing their processing order.
requirements.oracle: Check position-by-position values with unequal sentinels. Do not pair elements merely because their subscripts have the same numeric value, or require a particular traversal order. Snapshot effects remain required when the two sides overlap.

requirements.title: Numeric assignment to integer uses integer conversion
requirements.definition: Numeric RHS values assigned to an integer destination are converted as by `INT` with the destination kind.
requirements.oracle: Choose representable inputs with independently known integer results. Check both signs and nonzero imaginary parts. A comparison with an explicit conversion is secondary evidence, not the sole oracle, since both paths might share the same compiler defect.

requirements.title: Numeric assignment to real uses real conversion
requirements.definition: Numeric RHS values assigned to a real destination are converted as by `REAL` with the destination kind.
requirements.oracle: Use exact representable values for basic cases, including a complex RHS with a nonzero imaginary part. Precision-sensitive cases need an oracle justified by the processor's numeric model and the conversion rules, not an assumed bit layout or unjustified universal rounding result.

requirements.title: Numeric assignment to complex uses complex conversion
requirements.definition: Numeric RHS values assigned to a complex destination are converted as by `CMPLX` with the destination kind.
requirements.oracle: Check both components and destination precision. In particular, real/integer sources must not leave an old imaginary component behind. An optional wide-kind case is not covered if the corresponding complex kind was not exercised.

requirements.title: BOZ assignment uses the destination conversion
requirements.source: p9; Table 10.9, integer and real rows.
requirements.definition: A BOZ literal assigned to an eligible integer or real destination is converted using the corresponding Table 10.9 conversion and destination kind.
requirements.oracle: Use bit strings valid for the chosen representation and the BOZ rules, with independent expected values where available. A real bit-pattern fixture needs a documented numeric profile; arbitrary bit patterns are not portable controls. This entry does not permit a BOZ assignment to complex, logical, or character.

requirements.title: Logical assignment converts kind while preserving truth
requirements.definition: Logical assignment permits differing kinds and converts the RHS logical value to the destination kind.
requirements.oracle: Check truth values through logical operations for supported kind pairs. Do not inspect an assumed integer encoding of true or false. Same-kind cases remain useful controls where additional kinds are absent.

requirements.title: Character assignment truncates an overlong RHS
requirements.definition: If the destination character length is shorter, assignment retains the leftmost characters that fit and discards the excess on the right.
requirements.oracle: Use a nonrepeating string and check exact destination contents and unaffected surrounding characters. Separate fixed-length/substring cases from whole deferred-length allocatables, whose length can instead change under -005 through -008.

requirements.title: Character assignment pads an underlength RHS
requirements.definition: If the destination character length is longer, assignment extends the RHS on the right with the applicable blank character.

pending.nondefault-kind-profile: Needs an independently justified processor-specific padding oracle.

requirements.oracle: Pre-fill the destination with nonblanks and check the padding positions explicitly. The portable baseline uses default character. Nondefault-kind expectations must respect the character model rather than assuming a universal padding code point. Whole deferred-length allocation is a separate path.

requirements.title: Character assignment converts character kind
requirements.definition: For eligible differing character kinds, each RHS character is converted through its `IACHAR` value and `ACHAR` of the destination kind.

pending.replacement-profile: Needs an independently justified processor-specific replacement oracle.

requirements.oracle: Use supported kinds and known representable characters for portable value checks. A character not representable in the destination needs a processor-specific expectation, not a hard-coded replacement such as `?`. Track unavailable-kind and unresolved-profile facets separately from passing cases.

requirements.title: Integer-to-enum assignment uses enum construction
requirements.definition: In an eligible intrinsic assignment from integer to an enum-type destination, conversion has the effect of that enum type's constructor applied to the RHS.
requirements.oracle: Establish the enum value and type using valid expressions under Table 10.8. In particular, do not use an arbitrary integer RHS that lacks the required enumerator primary. Do not generalize this rule to the distinct enumeration-type feature.

requirements.title: Cross-image opaque assignment leaves an undefined value
requirements.definition: Assignment of C_PTR, C_FUNPTR, or TEAM_TYPE leaves the destination undefined when the destination and RHS are on different images.
requirements.oracle_limitation: There is no portable direct value assertion for the undefined result. Retain this gap instead of asserting nullness, a trap, or a particular bit pattern. A conforming wrapper-component copy can exercise the context without reading the resulting opaque component; that does not prove that the component was made undefined. Same-image controls likewise do not cover the cross-image effect.
requirements.dependencies: C915 rules out a naive direct coindexed designator. Concrete contexts require careful wrapper types, valid initial values, and multiple images. Do not read an undefined component through an inquiry, comparison, or representation-transfer workaround.

requirements.title: Derived-type pointer components use pointer assignment
requirements.source: p15, pointer-component branch; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: Corresponding pointer components are assigned using pointer assignment semantics rather than copying their targets' values.
requirements.oracle: Check association to a live source target, or disassociation for a defined disassociated source. For data pointers, mutate the still-live target through one alias and observe the other. Do not deep-copy the target or inspect a component whose association status is undefined.

requirements.title: Ordinary components use matching type-bound defined assignment
requirements.source: p15, nonpointer nonallocatable defined-assignment branch; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: A nonpointer nonallocatable component uses a consistent type-bound defined assignment when its type provides one.
requirements.oracle: Use a binding with an unmistakable controlled value effect. Confirm that the outer statement remains intrinsic assignment, and that the applicable component binding, not an unrelated generic assignment, accounts for the result. Do not require a global component-callback order.

requirements.title: Other ordinary components use intrinsic assignment
requirements.source: p15, remaining nonpointer nonallocatable components; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: Other nonpointer nonallocatable components are assigned intrinsically from the corresponding source components.
requirements.oracle: Give components distinguishable values and check recursive assignment effects. A nested component may in turn require one of the other dispatch rules. A test must not assume the entire object can always be implemented as a raw representation copy.

requirements.title: Allocated coarray components use intrinsic assignment
requirements.source: p15, allocated-coarray-component branch; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: An allocated coarray component is assigned intrinsically from its corresponding source component.
requirements.oracle: Establish conforming allocations, shapes, and parameters first, then check local assigned values on each image. Follow the coarray allocation and synchronization requirements. This is not the noncoarray allocatable deallocate-and-copy sequence in -029 through -032, nor permission to assign to an unallocated coarray.

requirements.title: An unallocated source coarray requires an unallocated destination
requirements.source: p15, sentence about unallocated coarray components.
requirements.definition: When the source coarray component is unallocated, the corresponding destination component must be unallocated.

pending.allocated-destination-unallocated-source: Needs a separately specified diagnostic-policy tier.

requirements.oracle: The positive control keeps both components unallocated. The mismatched-state case belongs only to a separately specified diagnostic-policy tier. Do not interpret the restriction as an instruction to automatically deallocate an allocated destination coarray component.

requirements.title: Noncoarray allocatable components discard an old allocation
requirements.source: p15, noncoarray allocatable sequence, item (1), with item (2)'s source-allocation condition.
requirements.definition: An allocated noncoarray allocatable destination component is deallocated first. If the source component is unallocated, no subsequent allocation or value assignment occurs, leaving the destination unallocated.
requirements.oracle: Check allocation status for the first two facets. For allocated sources, distinguish this sequence from a top-level no-trigger assignment using carefully scoped lifecycle observations where permitted by 7.5.6. Account for RHS temporaries and other finalization events; storage addresses and reads through invalidated pointers are not valid evidence.

requirements.title: Allocated source components establish matching allocations
requirements.source: p15, item (2), allocation and array-bounds provisions.
requirements.definition: An allocated noncoarray allocatable source component causes allocation of the destination component with matching dynamic type and type parameters and, for an array, matching bounds, before value assignment.
requirements.oracle: Use intrinsic-copy fixtures, or controlled bindings that do not alter the allocation characteristics, to inspect allocation state, metadata, and independent storage effects. Mutate an ordinary data value owned by the destination allocation and verify that the source is unaffected. Do not confuse that value with a target reached through a copied pointer component, which can legitimately remain shared under -024. The metadata is specified for the allocation step; a later user-defined assignment can have its own effects.

requirements.title: Allocatable component values can use defined assignment
requirements.source: p15, item (2), defined-assignment branch; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: After allocation, a noncoarray allocatable component's value is assigned using a consistent type-bound defined assignment if the component's declared type provides one.
requirements.oracle: Use a controlled binding to distinguish dispatch from an intrinsic copy, while respecting the binding's interface and intent semantics. Do not infer this branch merely from the presence of a binding available only in the dynamic type.

requirements.title: Other allocatable component values use dynamic-type intrinsic assignment
requirements.source: p15, item (2), fallback branch; qualified by p16.
requirements.definition: Otherwise, the allocated noncoarray component receives intrinsic assignment for its dynamic type.
requirements.oracle: Check the full dynamic-type payload, including extension components, and recursive component behavior. A declared-type-only shallow copy must not lose extension data. Verify that a dynamic-only binding does not incorrectly select the preceding defined-assignment branch.
